name: SkySense (Team Twisters)
tagline: Ultra-local, personalized weather risk from NASA Earth observation data, with the safest time window for your activity.
problem: People planning outdoor events, sports or travel get generic, unreliable forecasts rather than a personal answer for their place and time.
solution: A web app that combines NASA Earth observation data with AI analysis for ultra-local predictions of rain, wind, temperature, humidity and visibility, real-time risk assessments and suggested safest time windows, plus a conversational assistant (TwisterBot) that sends adaptive alerts and reminders.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the most innovative use of technology.
Turns weather variables into a decision: a real-time risk assessment plus the safest time window for an activity.
Grounded in named NASA sources (POWER API, Earthdata, Giovanni, GES DISC) alongside Open-Meteo, with a Gemini-powered assistant for alerts.

Submission package is complete: live product URL, demo video, data list and a specific AI-use disclosure (code assistance, design-to-code, icon generation) that separates the team's own work from tool help.
Answers the challenge's playful question literally, for one person and one plan, which makes the product understandable in a sentence.

lessons: Convert raw data into the one decision the user wants (when is it safe?).
For everyday-data challenges, personal and local beats global and generic.
Write the AI-use disclosure as carefully as the pitch: say what the tools did and what the team built.
LATAM precedent: a team from Mexico won a global technology award.

sources.note: Team-written summary, project details, AI-use disclosure, NASA and other data used.
